summary:
LUNA NAV (Lunar Landing Site Navigator) is an interactive web prototype designed to help users explore and compare potential lunar landing regions, with a focus on the Moon's south polar region.

The prototype provides a schematic locator with three illustrative candidate sites, site selection through map markers or a dropdown, approximate coordinate displays, a mission-date selector, and a comparison table. It introduces key factors relevant to lunar landing-site planning, including sunlight availability, direct-to-Earth communication visibility, and terrain conditions.

LUNA NAV aims to make lunar mission-planning concepts easier to understand through a simple, accessible browser-based interface. The current version demonstrates the exploration and comparison workflow; it does not yet perform scientific calculations or use live lunar terrain data. Future development will integrate verified NASA and JPL resources to support evidence-based illumination, communication visibility, and terrain analysis.
details:
Project: LUNA NAV – Lunar Landing Site Navigator

What does it do?

LUNA NAV is a browser-based prototype for exploring and comparing potential lunar landing regions. It provides a schematic locator, candidate-site selection, coordinate displays, a mission-date control, and a comparison table.

How does it work?

Users can select one of three illustrative candidate regions using the map markers or dropdown menu. The interface displays the selected site's coordinates and illustrative information. Users can also compare the candidate sites and select a mission date.

What problem does it address?

Lunar landing-site planning involves several important considerations, including sunlight availability for surface operations and solar power, visibility of Earth for communication, and terrain conditions that may affect landing safety.

What is its intended impact?

LUNA NAV aims to make lunar exploration and landing-site planning concepts more accessible. It provides a starting point for understanding and comparing the factors that future lunar missions need to evaluate.

Technology used

  • HTML – webpage structure
  • CSS – interface design and responsive styling
  • JavaScript – interactive features
  • Leaflet – schematic map interaction
  • GitHub Pages – public website hosting

Creativity and future development

The project combines site exploration and comparison in one accessible interface. Future development will focus on integrating verified NASA lunar datasets and JPL resources to support actual sunlight calculations, Earth visibility analysis, and terrain assessment.

Current scope

This is an early-stage interactive prototype. Its candidate locations and displayed conditions are illustrative and should not be interpreted as scientifically verified landing-site assessments.
